title: Crates re-organization
description:
# Crates re-organization

## Provenance

Created 2026-11-09 as a new tracker record for the documented target. Rewritten 2026-11-13 after the maintainer asked for the epic to be reviewed adversarially, corrected, shown and executed. Reviews: docs/reviews/crate-split-adversarial-review.md (first proposal) and docs/reviews/crate-split-plan-review.md (this plan). The design is docs/design/crate-split-plan.md. Its decisions D2-D16 are the author's defaults; the maintainer may overrule any of them.

## Goal

Split the single library into packages under crates/: frost-collections-core, frost-collections-integer, frost-collections-concurrent and the facade frost-collections, whose Rust import stays frost; plus the dev-only frost-collections-test-support. The graph is acyclic: integer on core, concurrent on core and optionally integer, the facade on all. Preserve every semantic and safety contract in docs/maintainers/implementation-contracts.md: representative identity, ownership, iterator, integer-storage and snapshot contracts, fixed freeze/thaw partners, every seal, additive features, no_std/core/alloc/std support, unsafe confined to one file, Rust 1.99.1 edition 2024. Every current public frost:: path keeps resolving unless a change is listed in the migration table. Publish nothing.

## Sequence

frost-wlt.1 plan and review; .7 move-safety gates; .8 workspace scaffold; .9 core; .11 integer; .12 concurrent; .13 tests and benches; .14 isolated harnesses; .15 orchestration; .16 parity; .17 documents; .6 evidence.

## Out of scope

An adaptive package (frost-adp: it needs the serde seal opened, a contract change only the maintainer can approve). Separating the families from core, a kernels crate, an algebra crate, any behaviour change, any publication. Known defects are tracked separately: frost-r0a, frost-k4n.

## Acceptance

- Every current module, test, benchmark, example and harness has one owner and was moved there. git diff -C --find-copies-harder reports no copied source file; no production algorithm exists twice.
- No test is weakened, skipped or deleted to pass. Test counts match the baseline by the rule in each task; differences are rows of the migration table.
- The public item paths under frost::, with inherent items and implemented traits, equal the baseline for each profile except for rows of the migration table.
- Seals stay private to the package that defines the sealed trait. Every foreign-trait implementation satisfies the orphan rule without a shim.
- Each package follows the standard layout of CRATES.md section 1.
- Core-only, alloc-only, std, each isolated feature, both embedded builds, the extracted-package test, the downstream codec check, and the Miri, Loom and Kani lanes were run against the final layout with versions and limits recorded. A lane not run blocks closing unless the maintainer waives it in docs/design/decisions.md.
- The union of catalog case IDs equals the 397 present before the move; make catalog passes for the workspace.
- No placeholder package and no unsupported performance or proof claim.

## Relationship

frost-wou.6 to .9 are re-based on this layout after frost-wlt.6. frost-wou.10 stays open; frost-wlt.14 checks dependency isolation by hand. frost-wlt no longer waits for frost-wou (decision D2).

title: Record, review and show the split plan
description:

Have readers who did not write the plan review it adversarially, with compile spikes, and resolve every finding.

Acceptance: docs/reviews/crate-split-plan-review.md lists each finding with its disposition, and each finding S01-S25 of the first review; a receipt of the crates.io name check is committed; make doc-links passes; the tracker tasks match the plan; superseded tasks .2-.5 are closed as superseded, not reused; the maintainer was shown the corrected epic and the list of defaults D2-D16 before any file moved.

Name receipt committed. The corrected epic and the defaults D2-D16 were shown to the maintainer in the session of 2026-11-13 before any file moved. make doc-links passed (1,206 links).

title: Record verification evidence for the migrated source
description:
After the extraction, artifact, harness, orchestration, parity and document tasks converge, run the complete applicable matrix and record new evidence against the final source revision.

Acceptance: make check and make verify, the feature and embedded gates, the downstream codec check, and the Miri, Loom, Kani and other ownership and model checks have receipts with tool versions, bounds and limitations; a lane that could not run is recorded as not run with the reason and blocks closing unless waived (decision D16); relevant benchmarks keep comparable native controls and raw observations; coverage is remeasured with unchanged or explicitly reviewed denominators. Pre-migration results are not reused as proof for moved code. Review findings are resolved before the epic closes. Miri is not run in the execution session (maintainer instruction of 2026-11-14); its lanes are recorded as not run and left to CI.
notes: 2026-11-14, second pass: evidence is in verification/results/crate-split/README.md, sections 'Final layout' and 'After the final layout'. Now run: fuzz-smoke on both targets (it found a fuzz-oracle defect that predates the split; corrected, seed and replay test added), cargo-mutants on one file per library package with identical outcomes before and after the split, benchmarks by two methods with controls, and GitHub CI. CI run 31 passes all 11 jobs on 237b3c6, including the three hosts and the ownership job, which runs make miri. CI had found a Windows-only defect in make catalog-inventory introduced by b28862b; fixed with Bats cases. Still open before this task can close (decision D16 needs the maintainer): (1) whether CI's make miri run satisfies the Miri lane, which was not run on the execution host by instruction; (2) the exact coverage ratchet baseline must be re-recorded on the reference host; (3) make verus was not run on this host; (4) make kani as a whole fails on two harnesses that did not finish before the split either (frost-k4n); (5) the plan is executed but not approved by the maintainer.

title: Put move-safety gates in place before any move
description:
Before any file moves, make the move checkable.

1. Baseline from the single-package tree, under verification/results/crate-split/baseline/: public item paths with inherent items and implemented traits, and executed test counts per target, for the all-features, default, alloc, core-only and int-set profiles; results of make check, profiles, features, embedded and bounded.
2. Every compile_fail doctest in src/ and README.md names an error code, except those whose error has none; for those the actual compiler error is recorded. make doctest-codes checks the codes with the pinned nightly.
3. Each lane that selects tests by name fails when a selected test binary executes zero tests, shown failing on an empty selection.
4. C-INLINE-OWNERSHIP, C-INT-SET-POLICY-LIMITS and C-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION each have a curated case with a stated oracle.
5. The host prerequisites are installed, or each missing tool is recorded with the lanes it blocks (plan section 9).

Acceptance: all five hold; the Miri lanes that cover src/adaptive/seq/buf.rs pass on the baseline tree; make check passes; no test body changed.
close_reason: Baselines for five profiles committed under verification/results/crate-split/baseline (413 tests under all features; API path lists). Four compile_fail doctests gained error codes; the four without a code have their compiler error recorded; make doctest-codes passed on nightly-2026-11-08 (60 doctests). scripts/require-tests.sh fails an empty selection per test binary, covered by two shell tests (39 pass). The three uncurated contracts each have a curated case. Installed: pinned nightly with Miri, both embedded targets, ShellCheck, shfmt, Bats, ast-grep, cargo-nextest, cargo-llvm-cov; not installed: cargo-mutants, cargo-fuzz, Verus. make check, profiles, features, embedded, bounded and two Miri lanes over buf.rs passed on the baseline tree. No test body changed.

title: Workspace scaffold: move the package unchanged
close_reason: Root is a virtual workspace; the package moved to crates/frost-collections with 131 exact renames (git diff -M100%), no Rust source line changed. Catalog tool reads a root catalog plus one per package (16 tool tests); all 397 prior case IDs are present, plus T-MAIN-015 and -016 for the new tool tests. make package tests a scratch workspace (decision D13). Link checker covers crates/ (1,221 links). Passed: make check, verify parts (profiles, features over 20 features, integers, examples, package), embedded, bounded, loom, fuzz-check, doctest-codes, shell-check (40 cases), tools-check, and the two Miri lanes over buf.rs. Test counts identical to the baseline in all five profiles. Not run: make miri in full, kani, nextest, coverage, mutants, fuzz-smoke. Open for .15: prepare-baseline.sh accepts only pre-workspace baselines; prose path mentions outside links are updated in .17.

title: Extract frost-collections-core
description:
Move everything the plan assigns to core (all of src except integer and concurrent, and the capability-trait implementations for dashmap, scc and crossbeam-skiplist types, decision D9) to crates/frost-collections-core. The facade keeps integer and concurrent, depends on core, re-exports it explicitly, and gains dev-dependencies, without default features, for the optional crates its tests, benches and examples name directly (decision D7). Items the facade's remaining modules need become #[doc(hidden)] pub behind core's __private module (decision D8); the list is closed by compiling and recorded in the migration table. Unsafe stays denied in core and allowed only in src/adaptive/seq/buf.rs, which moves as a unit with its safety comments. Core's unit-test catalog records move to core's catalog with IDs unchanged.

Acceptance: core builds alone for core-only, alloc and std and for both embedded targets; no seal is opened: frozen::sealed, Frozen::new_unchecked and the serde seal stay private to core; git diff -C --find-copies-harder reports no copied source file; the Kani package includes the moved buf.rs by path and its native helper tests pass; the Miri lanes that cover buf.rs pass; fixed freeze and thaw partners are unchanged; tests, benches and examples are unchanged and still run at the facade. Gates: make verify, make embedded, make bounded, make loom, make fuzz-check and make doctest-codes pass. Per profile (all-features, default, alloc, core-only, int-set) the multiset of (integration target, passed, ignored) equals the baseline of frost-wlt.7, the unit-test and doctest sums over packages equal the baseline, and failed is 0; any difference is a row of the migration table. cargo tree -e features shows core without std in the alloc, core-only and int-set lanes. CHANGELOG and the migration table in docs/design/crate-split-plan.md are updated in the same change. A lane whose tool is missing is recorded as not run (decision D16).
close_reason: frost-collections-core holds everything except the integer and concurrent modules, plus the capability implementations for dashmap, scc and crossbeam-skiplist types. Hidden interface __private (rejected, set_ops wrappers); no item became pub at its definition and no seal changed. Public paths, inherent items and trait implementations under frost:: are identical to the baseline in all five profiles (api_paths.py). Test counts: integration and unit identical, doctests split between the two libraries with equal sums, in all five profiles. No copied source file (git diff -C --find-copies-harder). Passed: make check, profiles, features (39 package-feature pairs), feature-isolation, integers, examples, package, embedded, bounded (Kani native helpers on the moved buf.rs), loom, fuzz-check, doctest-codes, shell-check (43 cases), tools-check, and both Miri lanes over buf.rs. Not run: make miri in full, kani solver, nextest, coverage, mutants.

The private Shared alias and both the atomic and non-atomic builds are kept. The integer unit-test catalog records move to the package's catalog with IDs unchanged.

close_reason: src/integer moved to crates/frost-collections-integer as module integer, depending on core only; the root re-exports core and defines its own prelude. title: Extract frost-collections-concurrent and reduce the facade to re-exports
description:
Move the live-access traits and implementations, snapshot publication and its seal to crates/frost-collections-concurrent as module concurrent, depending on core and optionally integer. It defines prelude and backend locally (decision D6). The facade then contains only explicit re-exports, the complete prelude and backend modules, feature forwarding and its README as crate documentation (CR-BOUND-2), with #![forbid(unsafe_code)].

Acceptance: the SnapshotValue seal and every seal implementation are in the concurrent package and private to it; tests/publication_model.rs and the Loom package include the moved publication.rs by path and make loom passes; int-set forwarding through the concurrent package works with and without arc-swap-1; a recipe fails when a layer does not forward a feature the layer below declares; frost::__private does not resolve; ambiguous_glob_reexports and hidden_glob_reexports are denied and clean. Gates: make verify, make embedded, make bounded, make loom, make fuzz-check and make doctest-codes pass. Per profile (all-features, default, alloc, core-only, int-set) the multiset of (integration target, passed, ignored) equals the baseline of frost-wlt.7, the unit-test and doctest sums over packages equal the baseline, and failed is 0; any difference is a row of the migration table. cargo tree -e features shows core without std in the alloc, core-only and int-set lanes. CHANGELOG and the migration table in docs/design/crate-split-plan.md are updated in the same change. A lane whose tool is missing is recorded as not run (decision D16). Miri is not run in the execution session (maintainer instruction of 2026-11-14); its lanes are recorded as not run and left to CI.
close_reason: src/concurrent moved to crates/frost-collections-concurrent as module concurrent, depending on core and optionally integer; it defines backend and prelude locally. The facade is named re-exports, backend, prelude and crate documentation only, with #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. The SnapshotValue seal and its implementations are unchanged and private to the concurrent package. tests/publication_model.rs and the Loom package include the moved publication.rs; make loom passes. A compile_fail,E0432 doctest shows frost::__private does not resolve. Workspace lints deny ambiguous_glob_reexports and hidden_glob_reexports; make feature-forwarding fails on a dropped forward (two shell tests). Public paths, inherent items and trait implementations under frost:: are identical to the baseline in all five profiles. Test counts equal the baseline plus the one new doctest in every profile. The four compile_fail doctests without an error code still fail with the recorded error. Passed: make check, profiles (with feature-isolation and feature-forwarding), features (78 package-feature pairs), integers, examples, package, embedded, bounded, loom, fuzz-check, doctest-codes, shell-check (45 cases), tools-check. Not run: Miri (maintainer instruction), kani solver, nextest, coverage, mutants.

title: Move tests and benches to their owning packages
description:
Create frost-collections-test-support from tests/support/workload.rs and benches/support/mod.rs (decision D12). Move each test and bench target to its owner by the rule of decision D14: lowest package in which it compiles, same executed-test count, same resolved Frost features in every lane. A moved target changes only its crate alias line, its support imports and a gate on a feature its new package always has; test bodies do not change. A target whose cases separate cleanly by owner is split and the split is listed in the migration table: the arc-swap-1 cases of tests/integer_sets.rs and tests/integer_output.rs go to a target in the concurrent package. Examples stay in the facade. tests/formal_models moves to core. Catalog and inventory records move with their targets (decision D11).

Acceptance: every baseline target exists in exactly one package, or is a listed split whose counts sum to the baseline; the alloc-only integer lane and the i686 Miri lanes still run against a build of core without std, shown with cargo tree -e features; no package refers to another package's tests or benches directory; git diff -C --find-copies-harder reports no copied file; the union of catalog case IDs is unchanged and make catalog and make catalog-inventory pass. Gates: make verify, make embedded, make bounded, make loom, make fuzz-check and make doctest-codes pass. Per profile (all-features, default, alloc, core-only, int-set) the multiset of (integration target, passed, ignored) equals the baseline of frost-wlt.7, the unit-test and doctest sums over packages equal the baseline, and failed is 0; any difference is a row of the migration table. cargo tree -e features shows core without std in the alloc, core-only and int-set lanes. CHANGELOG and the migration table in docs/design/crate-split-plan.md are updated in the same change. A lane whose tool is missing is recorded as not run (decision D16). Miri is not run in the execution session (maintainer instruction of 2026-11-14); its lanes are recorded as not run and left to CI.
close_reason: frost-collections-test-support holds the workload factories and benchmark timing helpers (no Frost dependency, dev-dependency only). Test targets: 24 in core, 4 in integer, 5 in concurrent; bench targets: 4, 2 and 1; examples and nothing else in the facade. Three targets are split under the same names (integer_sets 33+2, integer_output 18+1, metadata_and_factories 11+1); test bodies moved verbatim; the concurrent halves carry copies of three small helpers. In every one of the five profiles the per-target counts of executed tests equal the baseline and doctests equal the baseline plus the one doctest added in .12. Public paths, inherent items and trait implementations under frost:: are identical to the baseline in all five profiles. The alloc-only integer lane runs in the integer package against core without std. Catalog: all 397 baseline IDs present (402 with five new records), records and benchmark inventory live with their targets; make catalog and catalog-inventory pass. git diff -C --find-copies-harder reports no copy made by this work (it pairs the moved publication_model.rs with an identical historical file under verification/revision2-integration, and two small catalog files with each other). Passed: make check, profiles, features (78 pairs), integers, examples, package, embedded, bounded, loom, fuzz-check, doctest-codes, shell-check, tools-check. Not run: Miri (maintainer instruction), kani solver, nextest, coverage, mutants.

title: Colocate isolated verification packages with their owners
description:
Move the Kani package and the Verus proofs to core; the fuzz package, whole, to the integer package as <package>/fuzz (it is one library whose two targets share code, and the integer package is the lowest package that depends on everything it uses); Loom to the concurrent package; int-key-downstream to the facade (decision D15). Each keeps its own manifest, [workspace] table and committed lockfile. Historical evidence under verification/ stays (CR-LAYOUT-8); only its path dependencies and stale lockfiles change.

Acceptance: #[path] includes compile against the relocated production files, not copies; the Kani proof names, fuzz target names and fuzz library test names equal those before the move; the diff of unwind and bound attributes is empty; cargo tree -e normal for every library package in the core-only, alloc and default profiles is saved and contains no proof, model or fuzz tool; no harness exists in two locations; package exclusions keep verification and fuzz directories out of each package file set; make bounded, make loom, make fuzz-check and the native Kani helper tests pass; each Kani harness recorded as verified in docs/verification.md verifies again; catalog records keep their IDs. Miri is not run in the execution session (maintainer instruction of 2026-11-14); its lanes are recorded as not run and left to CI.
close_reason: Kani and Verus moved to crates/frost-collections-core/verification; Loom to the concurrent package; int-key-downstream to the facade; the fuzz package, whole, to crates/frost-collections-integer/fuzz (not split: one library shared by both targets). Each keeps its manifest, [workspace] table and lockfile. #[path] includes compile against the packages own files. Harness sources moved with git mv, so proof, fuzz-target and test names and all unwind and bound attributes are unchanged. Normal dependency trees of the four library packages for three profiles are saved and contain no proof, model or fuzz tool. No package file set contains verification/ or fuzz/. Catalog records moved to package catalogs with IDs unchanged. Passed: make bounded (Kani native helpers), loom, fuzz-check, integers; the nine Kani harnesses recorded as verified verify again. Not run: Miri (maintainer instruction); make kani as a whole still does not pass (frost-k4n); make verus and fuzz-smoke (tools not installed).

title: Workspace orchestration, CI and tool configurations
description:
Finish the Makefile, CI workflows and tool configurations for the final layout: recipes discover packages, features and targets from cargo metadata with jq (CR-MAKE-2, CR-MAKE-4) and keep Bash 3.2 and GNU Make 3.81 compatibility; isolated-feature, profile and embedded lanes run per package; coverage, mutation, nextest and ast-grep configurations, the shell tests and the integer A/B harness name the new layout; the coverage baseline is re-recorded, not compared across layouts.

Acceptance: git grep for a root-relative src/, tests/, benches/ or examples/ path in Makefile, .github, .config, sgconfig.yml, scripts, verification/shell and verification/ast-grep returns nothing; make help and dry runs execute no Cargo command; a failing recipe step fails the target, shown by a shell test; the packages named by make -n verify equal the workspace members from cargo metadata; make shell-check passes on the minimum available Bash, or is recorded as not run under decision D16.
close_reason: git grep for a root-relative src/, tests/, benches/ or examples/ path in Makefile, .github, .config, sgconfig.yml, scripts, verification/shell and verification/ast-grep returns nothing. Recipes discover packages, features and targets from cargo metadata; profile and isolated-feature lanes run per library package (four; the support package has no features and is covered by the workspace test lanes); embedded lanes build the facade, which builds core and integer in their no-std profiles. make help and dry runs execute no Cargo command and failing steps fail the target (shell tests, 45 cases). Coverage scope, pinned ratchet scope and policy updated; the baseline is not re-recorded because this is not the reference host, and the policy says so. prepare-baseline.sh handles both layouts; make integer-ab ran with a workspace baseline under --locked and with origin/main under AB_LOCKED=. Passed: make shell-check, tools-check, nextest (353 tests), coverage-gate in portable-floor mode. Not run: make mutants (tool not installed), coverage-branch.

title: Facade API and feature parity
description:
For each profile of the baseline, regenerate the public item paths under frost:: with inherent items and implemented traits and compare with the baseline of frost-wlt.7. Every difference is fixed or listed in the migration table with its reason. Run make doctest-codes, and re-run the four compile_fail doctests that have no error code as ordinary doctests to confirm each still fails with the recorded error.

Acceptance: the lists are equal per profile except for migration-table rows; bounds, hashers, auto traits and freeze/thaw partners are unchanged as shown by the unchanged contract tests and compile_fail doctests; each isolated feature, core-only, alloc-only, std and both embedded integer builds pass.
close_reason: Public item paths under frost::, with inherent items and implemented traits, are identical to the baseline in all five profiles (api_paths.py; the tool now collects trait implementations written in another crate and prints an external re-export by the last segment of its source, and reproduces the baseline files unchanged). The only addition is hidden: frost_collections_core::__private, which does not resolve through frost (compile_fail,E0432 doctest). make doctest-codes passed (61 doctests); the four compile_fail doctests without an error code were re-run as ordinary doctests and fail with the recorded error. Contract tests and compile_fail doctests are unchanged. Each isolated feature (78 package-feature pairs), core-only, alloc-only, std and both embedded integer builds pass.

title: Package documents and repository policy for the final layout
description:
Give each package its README, CHANGELOG and the design documents for its contracts (CR-LAYOUT-9); keep repository-wide documents and the research corpus at the root. Make every rule change in section 6 of the plan. Update AGENTS.md, the implementation contracts, crate-layout, architecture and the root README to describe the workspace as it is. Mark the proposal superseded.

Acceptance: make doc-links covers package documents and passes; git grep finds no statement that the repository is one library package outside historical records; every row of section 6 of the plan is done.
close_reason: Each internal package has a README and a CHANGELOG; package-specific design and evidence documents moved into crates/frost-collections-{core,integer,concurrent}/docs; repository-wide documents, the algebra chapters, research and reviews stay at the root. AGENTS.md (agent-rules), implementation contracts, repository rules, GitHub workflow guide, CRATES.md, crate-layout, the root README and the library README describe the workspace as it is; the proposal is marked superseded. Rules listed in section 6 of the plan are updated; CR-API-1 itself is unchanged, and CR-BOUND-2 states that sibling roots and hidden items are not API. make doc-links covers package documents (1,266 links). A grep for single-package statements in current documents finds none outside records. Backticked source paths in current documents name the new locations; historical records keep theirs.

title: Crate structure, verification, and benchmark standards
description:
# Crate structure, verification, and benchmark standards

## Goal

Define and implement repository standards in CRATES.md for the crate re-organization: src, tests, benches, fuzzing, Loom, Rust-based formal verification, property tests, mutation testing, high public-API coverage, test/benchmark metadata and tags, and deterministic parameterized benchmark data factories.

This is a separate epic linked to crates re-organization epic frost-wlt. That migration depends on this standards epic. frost-wlt was created with explicit user authorization after the earlier epic could not be recovered; it is not presented as a recovered historical record. Package moves belong to frost-wlt, not this epic.

## Scope

- Use write-enabled NTM Opus, Fable, and Argon lanes with economical research subagents and current primary-source documentation.
- Establish a canonical crate directory and ownership standard in CRATES.md, update the repository guidance and design/maintenance entry points.
- Define risk-based API coverage, semantic obligations, feature/target matrices, mandatory gates, tool scopes, and explicit exceptions. Never report desired coverage as measured coverage.
- Add structured stable metadata/tags for tests and benchmarks, discoverability and validation, and parameterized reproducible workload factories with exact scenario guarantees and native controls.
- Specify and demonstrate Rust-based fuzz, property, mutation, Loom, Miri, and bounded/formal verification integration without adding these to normal runtime dependencies.
- Use NTM Terra to implement GitHub issue forms and PR templates aligned with the repository's evidence and verification requirements.

## Acceptance

- CRATES.md is the canonical linked standard, with target layout and current implementation state clearly distinguished.
- Test strategy covers public APIs, semantic laws, panic/ownership paths, feature combinations, portability, concurrency, and adversarial inputs; tags, manifests, reproducibility, and coverage/mutation accounting are concrete and checkable.
- Parameterized factory support has deterministic seeds, bounded generation, exact requested shapes or explicit rejection, correctness oracles, and replayable benchmark identifiers.
- Templates are valid and provide focused bug, feature/design, research, and PR information without secrets or unnecessary blanket checklists.
- Epic tasks, dependencies, and acceptance criteria reflect the final reviewed proposal and implementation; the re-organization relationship is recorded once its real ID is known.
- Relevant focused checks, make check, and any affected shell/feature/embedded gates pass, or actual blockers and remaining gates are explicitly recorded.

## Baseline

Repository commit 6ab0918dbbf655894d8d3176b81091bd28899c5f; Rust 1.99.1 edition 2024; one current library package with optional isolated verification packages. All four NTM lanes must preserve library semantic contracts and unrelated changes.
notes:
Reviewed plan: CRATES.md governs the current single package and the future flat crates/frost-* layout. Initial implementation is frost-wou.1 through frost-wou.5. Adoption follow-ups are frost-wou.6 (full API obligation curation), .7 (branch/profile and CI baselines), .8 (mutation baseline), .9 (high structural coverage targets), and .10 (automated dependency-isolation guards). The epic remains open until its adoption gates are satisfied; package moves remain in linked frost-wlt.
Implementation tasks frost-wou.1 through frost-wou.5 are complete with checked acceptance criteria. Evidence: verification/crate-standards-validation/README.md and after-coverage.json. Standards epic stays open for adoption tasks frost-wou.6 through frost-wou.10; reorganization epic frost-wlt remains dependent and its migration tasks remain open. No migration, commit, push, or GitHub workflow execution is claimed.

comments.author: CobaltFrog
comments.text: Measured baseline at 6ab0918: host aarch64 all-feature cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1 with Rust1.99.1 passed; source line coverage 7089/9183 (77.197%), function coverage1343/1894 (70.908%), regions11067/14230 (77.772%). Branches and semantic API obligation coverage are unmeasured. Durable sanitized observation: verification/crate-standards-validation/baseline-coverage.json. Coverage gap work is frost-wou.5. Target thresholds must remain distinct from this baseline.

title: Define CRATES.md and crate verification policy
description: Author canonical crate structure, lifecycle, ownership, metadata and coverage policy in CRATES.md; update guidance and linked design/maintenance docs; synthesize primary-source research and the other lanes; no package migration.

title: Automate verification dependency isolation checks
description:
# Automate verification dependency isolation checks

Turn the current isolated-package and cargo-tree evidence into a required dependency-leakage guard for the future workspace. Keep metadata parsing in Make recipes with jq.

Acceptance:
- Check normal dependency graphs for core-only, alloc-only and supported optional profiles.
- Reject accidental library dependencies on test, fuzz, model, proof or catalog tooling.
- Check each isolated harness remains independently buildable with its own lockfile and production linkage.
- Include negative fixtures for the guard without mutating the real library manifest during checks.

title: Implement tagged verification catalog and workload factories
description: Implement typed deterministic parameterized benchmark/test data factories, regression tests, test and benchmark metadata with stable IDs and tags, and validation/discovery tooling; preserve runtime dependencies.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Catalog validates stable metadata, controlled tags, source/target discovery and measured benchmark-case registration; negative fixtures reject drift. Legacy uncurated semantics remain explicit.
- [x] Deterministic factories reject invalid or oversized parameters before generation, preserve exact shapes and u64 boundary behavior, and drive real benchmarks with correctness oracles outside timing.
notes: Fable completed deterministic factories, boundary/preflight fixes, 12 factory regressions and 914 exact benchmark records. Remaining discovery/schema and portable inventory work transferred to Terra after Fable reported partial completion and became idle; root records the lease handoff in the round3 ledger.
close_reason: Implemented and validated the isolated Rust catalog, typed metadata, exact 922-case benchmark inventory, and deterministic factories. make check and isolated catalog Clippy passed. Semantic legacy API curation remains frost-wou.6.

title: Define Rust verification strategy and measurable gates
description: Research and implement the testing strategy for coverage, property testing, fuzzing, mutation, Loom, Miri and Rust formal frameworks; write source-backed tooling choices, honest current status and adoption gates.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Rust verification strategy and PR/nightly/release tiers match executable Make/CI commands, preserve isolation, and distinguish scoped measurements from targets and unrun tools.
- [x] Fuzz replay asserts nontrivial decoded fixtures and independent production oracles; both bounded smoke targets pass. Coverage adoption floors are not mislabeled as scoped baseline ratchets.
close_reason: Implemented Make/CI verification tiers, scoped coverage gate, strict fuzz oracles, nextest and mutation policy. Final make check, 35 shell cases under two Make versions, fuzz replay and both smoke targets, actual coverage-gate, and actionlint passed. Unavailable mutation/Kani and unrun release/CI scopes remain explicitly documented.

title: Add GitHub issue forms and PR template
description: Use Terra to implement and validate concise GitHub issue forms and a PR template reflecting repository contribution, evidence, scope and verification best practices; verify current official GitHub syntax.
acceptance_criteria: - [x] Valid concise issue forms and PR template request affected APIs, feature/target scope, metadata IDs and actual evidence; the workflow guide links CRATES.md and both epics without claiming GitHub rendering was tested.
close_reason: Terra implemented and synthesized all three issue forms, chooser, PR template and GitHub workflow guide. Root reviewed files; YAML/schema subset, whitespace and local link checks passed. GitHub rendering remains untested until publication to the default branch; no publication is claimed.

title: Close measured public API coverage gaps and document remaining obligations
description: Baseline Rust1.99.1 all-feature instrumented library source: 7089/9183 lines (77.197%), 1343/1894 functions (70.908%); no branch instrumentation. Add independent semantic API tests for ordinary family and capability gaps, annotate metadata, remeasure, and record the difference between measured executable coverage and contract/API inventory. No production API edits or lowered semantic expectations.
acceptance_criteria: - [x] Six additional API contract tests have independent oracles and explicit bounds, pass the relevant profiles, and have reviewed metadata plus same-scope before/after source coverage evidence.
close_reason: Added six independent public API contract tests and recorded final same-scope source coverage: lines 7269/9183, functions 1397/1894, regions 11303/14230. Feature matrix, profiles, embedded builds, make check and coverage gate passed. Bounds and remaining obligations are documented in verification/crate-standards-validation; high targets remain frost-wou.9.

title: Curate the complete public API obligation inventory
description:
# Curate the complete public API obligation inventory

Apply CRATES.md to every public item under the supported feature profiles. Distinguish discovered test/benchmark records from reviewed semantic evidence. Replace legacy scaffolded records with reviewed contracts, oracles, tags and source provenance; do not infer semantic coverage from test counts or textual symbol matches.

Acceptance:
- Inventory public API obligations by operation, ownership, representative, iterator, feature and concurrency contract, including uncovered obligations.
- Link each covered obligation to an asserting case and identify its actual feature/target scope.
- Preserve stable metadata IDs and record curated/scaffolded/uncovered counts explicitly.
- Run the isolated catalog validator and relevant tests; never weaken discovery to hide missing records.

This is standards adoption after the initial catalog infrastructure, not evidence that current semantic coverage is complete.

title: Measure branch and isolated-profile coverage
description:
# Measure branch and isolated-profile coverage

Record the first supported branch measurement and coverage for core-only, alloc-only and important isolated features. Match compiler, target, feature profile and denominator when comparing baselines. Establish a Linux CI baseline separately from the measured aarch64-apple-darwin baseline.

Acceptance:
- Preserve raw summaries, tool versions, commands, exclusions, covered/total counts and source identity.
- Keep unmeasured metrics explicit; no zero-denominator percentage claim.
- Establish scoped non-regression baselines independently of portable adoption floors.
- Set branch and profile targets only after reviewing actual measurements and justified exclusions.

title: Establish mutation baseline and triage survivors
description:
# Establish mutation baseline and triage survivors

Run the pinned mutation tool against priority public API algorithms using the configured deterministic tests. The initial implementation validates missing-tool failure, not a mutation score.

Acceptance:
- Record tool/compiler versions, source identity, selected files, test command and raw outcome artifacts.
- Triage every survivor, timeout and unviable mutant; add regression tests for genuine gaps.
- Equivalent-mutant and other waivers include the rationale and owner/review information required by CRATES.md.
- Report the precise score denominator and excluded outcomes; adopt a gate only after a reviewed baseline.

title: Reach high coverage targets with meaningful API tests
description:
# Reach the high coverage targets with meaningful API tests

Expand assertions in the low-coverage mutable family and native capability modules identified by the baseline. The initial six API regression tests improve specific obligations; they do not establish complete coverage.

Acceptance:
- Reach the proposed 90% source lines, 90% regions and 85% functions within explicitly matched measurement scopes, or document narrowly reviewed exceptions.
- Prioritize independent standard-library differential tests, bounded operation traces, representative retention, partial iteration and ownership/drop behavior.
- Link assertions to the curated API obligation inventory; do not add tests solely to execute lines or weaken production behavior.
- Raise adoption gates using reviewed evidence and preserve raw before/after results.

title: Decide whether to extract an adaptive package
description:
The crate split (frost-wlt) keeps the adaptive profiles in frost-collections-core. Extracting them into their own package would let every other package forbid unsafe code, but it requires: (1) the serde seal adapters::serde::private::Sealed, which StrictEntries and Canonical rely on, to be implemented from another crate, so it becomes #[doc(hidden)] pub and is no longer a seal; (2) eleven adapter macros and nine helpers in src/adapters to be exported and rewritten with $crate paths; (3) the freeze implementations for Inline and AdaptiveHash to move beside the plan types. Item 1 relaxes a contract, which the API-compatibility decision of 2026-11-12 does not permit without the maintainer.

Acceptance: the maintainer decides. If approved, a design record states the seal change and a task extracts the package with the gates of frost-wlt.9.

title: int-set exposes the Roaring adapter, against CR-DEP-1
description:
CR-DEP-1 says the int-set feature uses roaring privately and exposes no roaring type. The Roaring adapter and the frost::backend::roaring re-export are gated on any(roaring-0_12, int-set) (src/backends/bitmap.rs, src/backend.rs), so int-set alone exposes them. Found by the crate-split review (S06). The split preserves today's behaviour by giving the core package an int-set feature.

Acceptance: either the gate is narrowed to roaring-0_12 with a changelog entry, or CR-DEP-1 is corrected to describe the behaviour.

title: Two Kani harnesses do not finish
description:
Under Kani 0.68.0 on a 4-CPU, 15 GB host, ordered_set_algebra was stopped at 1,500 s and 10.3 GB, and dense_padding_does_not_create_members at 420 s (docs/verification.md, recorded run of 2026-11-13). The repository records no earlier solver run of either. Both build a Vec whose length depends on a symbolic value; the set_laws harnesses had the same problem until each operand was given a fixed-size allocation.

Acceptance: both harnesses verify on the reference host with stated bounds, or are replaced by harnesses that do, and make kani passes.

title: Eight mutants in plan.rs and policy.rs are not caught
description:
cargo-mutants 25.3.1 over crates/frost-collections-core/src/plan.rs and crates/frost-collections-integer/src/integer/policy.rs leaves eight mutants uncaught (verification/results/crate-split/final/mutants/split/missed.txt): the Display, Debug and Error::source implementations of Rejected, Display of LengthMismatch and of IntSetError, IntSetPolicy::max_roaring_partitions replaced by 0 and by 1, and one operator in the default dense budget of IntSetPolicy::auto. The same mutants were uncaught before the crate split, so this is not a regression.

Acceptance: each of the eight mutants is caught by a test with a catalog record, or is recorded as an accepted equivalent mutant with the reason.
